objects.description: Enumeration of TensorFlow Lite logging severities, from most verbose to silent. Used throughout TFLite logging APIs to select the minimum level of messages that will be emitted.
Configuration holder for TFLite logging. Provides static methods to get and set the global minimum logging severity. No instances are constructed; the API is purely static.

Internal helper for platform-specific minimal console-style logging. Exposes static logging functions and manages a static minimum severity threshold via a private static member. Not intended for direct construction or instance use.

functions.name: tflite::LoggerOptions::GetMinimumLogSeverity
functions.description: Returns the current minimum log severity for TensorFlow Lite logging. Intended for callers that need to check whether a given message should be emitted. Defaults are platform/build dependent (INFO in production, VERBOSE in debug, always VERBOSE on Android). This API is marked experimental and may change.
requirements: May be called at any time; no initialization required.
Return value is a tflite::LogSeverity in the range [TFLITE_LOG_VERBOSE, TFLITE_LOG_SILENT].
Behavior and default value are build/platform dependent as noted in the header comments (experimental API).

functions.name: tflite::LoggerOptions::SetMinimumLogSeverity
functions.description: Sets the process-wide minimum log severity for TensorFlow Lite logging and returns the previous severity. Use to raise or lower the verbosity threshold at runtime. This API is experimental and subject to change.
requirements: new_severity must be a valid tflite::LogSeverity enum value (TFLITE_LOG_VERBOSE through TFLITE_LOG_SILENT).
Affects subsequent logging calls globally; callers should consider process-wide impact.
Returns the previous minimum severity for possible restoration.

functions.name: tflite::logging_internal::MinimalLogger::Log
functions.signature: static void tflite::logging_internal::MinimalLogger::Log(tflite::LogSeverity severity, const char* format, ...);
functions.description: Prints a log message using a printf-style format string and variadic arguments at the given severity. Designed as a small, platform-specific console logger to minimize binary size. Typically used via the TFLITE_LOG/TFLITE_LOG_PROD macros which gate calls by the current minimum severity.
requirements: severity must be a valid tflite::LogSeverity value.
format must be a non-null, null-terminated printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers exactly (types, count, and modifiers).
Pointers referenced by the format or arguments must be valid for the duration of the call.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not documented; treat as unknown.
Logging emission may be gated by the configured minimum severity (commonly handled by macros).

functions.name: tflite::logging_internal::MinimalLogger::LogFormatted
functions.signature: static void tflite::logging_internal::MinimalLogger::LogFormatted(tflite::LogSeverity severity, const char* format, va_list args);
functions.description: Prints a pre-formatted va_list log message at the given severity using a printf-style format. Useful when forwarding an existing va_list. Typically used internally by logging helpers.
requirements: severity must be a valid tflite::LogSeverity value.
format must be a non-null, null-terminated printf-style format string compatible with args.
args must be a valid, initialized va_list corresponding to format (started with va_start in the caller).
Do not reuse args after this call unless you make a copy with va_copy, per va_list rules.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not documented; treat as unknown.
Logging emission may be gated by the configured minimum severity.

functions.name: tflite::logging_internal::MinimalLogger::GetMinimumLogSeverity
functions.description: Returns the current minimum severity threshold used by MinimalLogger to decide whether to emit messages. Defaults are build/platform dependent (INFO in prod, VERBOSE in debug; always VERBOSE on Android).
requirements: May be called at any time; no initialization required.
Return value is a tflite::LogSeverity in the range [TFLITE_LOG_VERBOSE, TFLITE_LOG_SILENT].

functions.name: tflite::logging_internal::MinimalLogger::SetMinimumLogSeverity
functions.description: Sets the minimum severity threshold for MinimalLogger and returns the previous threshold. Use to adjust logging verbosity at runtime.
requirements: new_severity must be a valid tflite::LogSeverity value (TFLITE_LOG_VERBOSE through TFLITE_LOG_SILENT).
Affects subsequent logging calls globally within MinimalLogger; callers should consider process-wide impact.
Returns the previous minimum severity for possible restoration.

data_types.description: A generic byte string with no required encoding or structure. May contain any bytes including nulls when treated as a buffer, but when passed as a C string it is typically expected to be UTF-8 or printable text and null-terminated. Suitable for use as free-form log message content.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces interesting, valid byte strings intended for use as
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() inputs in the MinimalLogger::Log fuzzer stub. The stub
# treats the returned data as a C string via std::string::c_str(), so we should
# provide text-like payloads (including edge and boundary cases) that are still
# valid, printable, and exercise diverse formatting and size behaviors.
#
# Constraints/Goals:
# - Return bytes <= 4096 bytes.
# - Seeded determinism with variability per call.
# - Focus on valid strings that are safe with printf %s: no embedded nulls that
#   would prematurely terminate display (we avoid \x00 to keep messages intact).
# - Include varied sizes: empty, very short, typical words, long lines, multi-
#   line, whitespace-heavy, unicode (UTF-8), long repeating chars, hex-like,
#   JSON-like, format-like strings containing percent signs to exercise literal
#   percent printing in the format arguments (note: percent signs in the string
#   are safe because they are data for %s, not format specifiers).
# - Include addresses/hex patterns to make %p/%x-related logs human-discernible.

ASCII_PRINTABLE = (
    [c for c in range(0x20, 0x7F)]  # visible ASCII
)
WHITESPACE = [0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x20]  # \t\n\v\f\r space

# Some interesting Unicode snippets (UTF-8)
UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "こんにちは世界",           # Japanese
    "Привет, мир",            # Russian
    "안녕하세요 세계",          # Korean
    "مرحبا بالعالم",          # Arabic (RTL text)
    "γειά σου κόσμε",          # Greek
    "हैलो वर्ल्ड",            # Devanagari
    "你好，世界",               # Chinese
    "🌟✨🔥🚀",                 # Emojis
    "café naïve coöperate",  # Latin accents
]

JSON_TEMPLATES = [
    '{"msg":"%s","level":"%s","value":%d}',
    '{"event":"log","severity":"%s","data":{"k":"%s","n":%d}}',
]

WORDS = [
    "alpha","beta","gamma","delta","epsilon","zeta","eta","theta",
    "iota","kappa","lambda","mu","nu","xi","omicron","pi","rho",
    "sigma","tau","upsilon","phi","chi","psi","omega",
]

HEX_CHARS = "0123456789abcdef"


def _rand_bytes_printable(r: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Generate printable ASCII (and some whitespace), excluding NUL.
    spacey = ASCII_PRINTABLE + WHITESPACE
    return bytes(r.choice(spacey) for _ in range(length))


def _rand_word(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return r.choice(WORDS)


def _hex_str(r: random.Random, nbytes: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(r.choice(HEX_CHARS) for _ in range(nbytes * 2))


def _repeat_pattern(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    patterns = [
        "A", "0", " ", "-", "_", "=", "*", ".", "#", "%", "x",
        "ab", "01", "\t ", "\n", "XYZ", "1234", "deadbeef",
    ]
    p = r.choice(patterns)
    length = r.randrange(0, max(1, max_len // max(1, len(p))))
    return (p * length)[:max_len]


def _make_multiline(r: random.Random, lines: int, max_total: int) -> str:
    out: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(lines):
        L = r.randint(0, max(0, max_total // max(1, lines)))
        s = _rand_bytes_printable(r, L).decode('latin1')
        out.append(s)
    return "\n".join(out)


def _make_json_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    tmpl = r.choice(JSON_TEMPLATES)
    s1 = _rand_bytes_printable(r, r.randint(0, 40)).decode('latin1')
    s2 = _rand_bytes_printable(r, r.randint(0, 20)).decode('latin1')
    # Ensure we don’t include quotes that could break JSON-like appearance too much
    s1 = s1.replace('"', "'")
    s2 = s2.replace('"', "'")
    val = r.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1)
    return tmpl % (s1, _rand_word(r), val) if '%d' in tmpl else tmpl % (s1, _rand_word(r), val)


def _with_percents(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include literal percent signs to test payloads containing '%'
    parts = [
        "100% ready", "progress: 50%", "fmt: %s %d %p", "rate=%d%%", "%%escaped%%",
    ]
    base = r.choice(parts)
    tail = _rand_bytes_printable(r, r.randint(0, 40)).decode('latin1')
    return base + " " + tail


def _make_unicode(r: random.Random) -> str:
    s = r.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS)
    # Mix with ASCII
    prefix = _rand_bytes_printable(r, r.randint(0, 20)).decode('latin1')
    suffix = _rand_bytes_printable(r, r.randint(0, 20)).decode('latin1')
    return prefix + s + suffix


def _pick_case(r: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    # Ensure not exceeding budget (<= 4096 total)
    kind = r.randrange(10)
    if kind == 0:
        # Empty string
        return b""
    elif kind == 1:
        # Short word
        return _rand_word(r).encode('utf-8')
    elif kind == 2:
        # Long line of ASCII
        L = r.randint(64, min(1024, budget))
        return _rand_bytes_printable(r, L)
    elif kind == 3:
        # Multiline
        lines = r.randint(2, 20)
        s = _make_multiline(r, lines, min(budget, 1000))
        return s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    elif kind == 4:
        # JSON-like
        s = _make_json_like(r)
        return s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    elif kind == 5:
        # Hex dump style
        n = r.randint(8, min(256, budget // 2))
        s = _hex_str(r, n)
        return s.encode('ascii')
    elif kind == 6:
        # Repeated pattern
        s = _repeat_pattern(r, min(budget, 1500))
        return s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    elif kind == 7:
        # With percents
        s = _with_percents(r)
        return s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    elif kind == 8:
        # Unicode mix
        s = _make_unicode(r)
        return s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    else:
        # Address-like and numbers to pair with %p %zu %s
        addr = '0x' + _hex_str(r, 8)
        size = r.randint(0, 1 << 20)
        msg = _rand_bytes_printable(r, r.randint(0, 200)).decode('latin1')
        s = f"ptr={addr} size={size} msg={msg}"
        return s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Optionally bias selection to exercise boundaries and variety
    outputs: List[bytes] = []

    # Include a few diverse candidates and pick one to keep output size bounded
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
        outputs.append(_pick_case(r, 4096))

    # Join choices with newline to keep it as single string, but ensure total <= 4096
    joined = b"\n".join(outputs)
    if len(joined) > 4096:
        joined = joined[:4096]
    # Avoid embedding NUL to keep %s printing full payload; replace if any
    if b"\x00" in joined:
        joined = joined.replace(b"\x00", b"?")
    return joined
